JOHN ADAMS, PRESIDENT of the  
UNITED STATES of AMERICA.
_________
To ________ Marshal for the District of ________ or his 
Deputy, GREETING:
WHEREAS by an Act of Congress, intituled, “An 
Act concerning Aliens,” passed on the twenty-fifth day 
of June, one thousand seven hundred and ninety-
eight, it is enacted, That it shall be lawful for the 
President of the United States to order all such Aliens 
as he shall judge dangerous to the peace and safety of 
the United States, or shall have reasonable grounds to 
suspect are concerned in any treasonable or secret 
machinations against the government thereof, to 
depart out of the territory of the United States, within 
such time as shall be expressed in such order:  AND 
WHEREAS it appears to me, That
________
and an alien to the United States, is a person within 
the meaning and description of the aforesaid Act, and 
that his longer residence within the United States will 
endanger their peace and safety: NOW THEREFORE, 
I do hereby require you to give notice to the said 
________ that he depart, and he is hereby ORDERED 
to depart out of the territory of the United States, 
within ________ days after a copy of this order shall be 
delivered to him, or left at his usual abode: BUT

2a 
WHEREAS it is provided by the aforesaid Act, That if 
any alien, ordered in pursuance thereof, to depart from 
the territory of the United States, shall prove, to the 
satisfaction of the President, by evidence to be taken 
before such person or persons, as the President shall 
direct, and who for that purpose are authorized to 
administer oaths, that no injury or danger to the 
United States will accrue from suffering such alien to 
reside therein, the President may grant a licence to 
such alien to remain within the United States, for such 
time as he shall judge proper, and at such place as he 
may designate: NOW THEREFORE I do hereby also 
require you to give notice to the said ________ that he 
may appear, if he see fit, at any time within ________ 
days prior to the expiration of the period above limited 
for his departure from the United States, before

APPENDIX B 
_________
(15275.)
Arrest and deportation of an alien contract laborer.
TREASURY DEPARTMENT, 
OFFICE OF SUPERINTENDENT OF IMMIGRATION,
Washington, D. C., September 17, 1894.
SIR: The bureau is in receipt of your letter of 
September 15, 1894, No. 2156, in which you transmit 
papers in the case of Henry W. Elliott, aged 29, who 
arrived as a first-cabin passenger, per steamship 
Berlin, August 20, 1894. From a careful examination 
of the affidavits transmitted, the Department is of the 
opinion that the said Elliott previous to his 
embarkation from London for the United States 
entered into a contract with Mr. Augustin Daly to 
perform labor and services as property man in the 
theater belonging to said Daly, known as “Daly’s 
Theater,” in the city of New York. It moreover appears 
from the evidence submitted that said Elliott upon 
arrival went to his destination, and has in fact worked 
pursuant to said contract made prior to his landing, 
and has been paid for said work at the rate of $30 per 
week by said Daly. It also appears that the matter has 
been carefully investigated by James McKim, 
immigrant inspector, under the direction of the 
Commissioner of Immigration at the port of New 
York.
The case has been presented to the honorable the 
Secretary of the Treasury, and he being satisfied that

5a 
the immigrant has been allowed to land contrary to 
the provisions of the Alien Contract-Labor Law, has 
caused his warrant to be issued for the arrest and 
deportation to the country whence he came of the said 
Henry W. Elliott, as provided by law. Said warrant is 
addressed to James McKim, immigrant inspector, and 
inclosed herewith. After arrest and prior to 
deportation the deposition of the said Henry W. Elliott 
should be taken, and together with all the papers in 
the case, and such other evidence as you may be able 
to gather, submitted to the U. S. district attorney for 
the district in which the alleged violation has 
occurred, and suit instituted against the contractor to 
recover the penalties prescribed by law.
Respectfully, yours,
FRANK H. LARNED,
Acting Superintendent.
COMMISSIONER OF I MMIGRATION, Ellis Island, New 
York.
_________
WARRANT.
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,
Washington, D. C., September 17, 1894.
Whereas, from proofs submitted to me, I have 
become satisfied that Henry W. Elliott, an alien 
immigrant who landed in the United States at the 
port of New York on the 20th day of August, 1894, 
came into this country from London, England, 
contrary to the prohibition of the acts of Congress

6a 
approved February 26, 1885, February 23, 1887, 
October 19, 1888, and March 3, 1891, commonly 
known as the Alien Contract-Labor Laws; and 
whereas, the period of one year after landing has not 
elapsed:
I, John G. Carlisle, Secretary of the Treasury of the 
United States, by virtue of the power and authority 
vested in me by the above cited acts of Congress, do 
hereby command you to take into custody the said 
Henry W. Elliott, alien immigrant, and return him to 
the country whence he came at the expense of the 
vessel importing him.
For so doing, this shall be your sufficient warrant.
Witness my hand and seal this 17th day of 
September, 1894.
[SEAL.] J. G. CARLISLE,
Secretary of the Treasury.
Mr. JAMES MCKIM,
U. S. Immigrant Inspector.

7a 
APPENDIX C 
_________
BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION
Form 8-A
WARRANT—ARREST OF ALIEN
_________
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
Department of Commerce and Labor
Washington
No. 51,320-2/A
To JOHN H. CLARK, Commissioner of Immigration, 
Montreal, Canada. 
Or any Immigrant Inspector in the service of the 
United States.
WHEREAS, from evidence submitted to me, it 
appears that
MAGDALENE GLINDEMANN, aged 16, native 
of Germany,
alien who landed at the port of New York per S.S. 
“Kaiserin Auguste Victoria” on the 11th day of Aug. 
1906, has been found in the United States in violation 
of the Act of Congress approved March 3, 1903, to wit:
That said alien entered the United States without 
inspection as prescribed by the above mentioned Act, 
and is reported to be at River Rouge, Michigan;
I, V. H. METCALF, Secretary of Commerce and 
Labor, by virtue of the power and authority vested in 
me by the laws of the United States, do hereby

8a 
command you to take into custody the said alien and 
convey her before an officer designated by you to 
enable her to show cause why she should not be 
deported in conformity with law. After conclusion of 
such hearing, the alien will be released from custody 
and paroled upon her own recognizance pending 
further action of the Department.
The preliminary papers in this case are 
transmitted herewith for your information, and 
should be returned with report of the hearing to be 
held hereunder.
The expenses incident to the execution of this 
warrant are hereby authorized.
For so doing, this shall be your sufficient warrant.
Witness my hand and seal this 4th day of October, 
1906.
V. H. Metcalf
[Signature]
Secretary of Commerce and Labor.
